name: GUINEA

flag.title: Red, Gold & Green
flag.note: Red, gold, green — work, justice, solidarity

lead: Guinea sits on the coast of West Africa. Its hills feed the Niger, Gambia and Senegal rivers. Under the red soil lies the biggest store of bauxite, the ore for aluminium. The djembe drum began in its villages.

facts.label: Land area
facts.sub: About the same size as the UK

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Guinea has four zones. The coast has mangrove swamps. Inland, the Fouta Djallon plateau has cool grasslands, gorges and waterfalls. Its water feeds rivers across West Africa.
The Forest Region in the south-east is thick jungle full of chimpanzees. Mount Nimba, a UNESCO nature reserve, protects hundreds of species found nowhere else.
animals: Guinea's forests shelter one of the biggest groups of western chimpanzees. In Bossou village, wild chimps crack nuts with stones. Mothers teach their babies.
The shy pygmy hippo hides in swampy lowlands. A toad on Mount Nimba gives birth to live tadpoles. Few amphibians do that.
culture: The djembe is a goblet-shaped drum that began in Mandinka villages. Griots are storyteller-musicians. They memorise royal histories and sing them at weddings and festivals.
Rice with peanut sauce is an everyday meal, eaten from a shared bowl. The Pular, Malinke and Susu peoples each have their own language and music.
history: On 2 October 1958, Guinea became the first French colony to vote for independence. Leader Sékou Touré said: 'We prefer poverty in freedom to riches in slavery.'
Touré ruled harshly for 26 years. After he died in 1984, Guinea slowly opened up. Its bauxite makes it one of Africa's most important countries.
wows: Guinea holds the world's largest bauxite reserves.
The Fouta Djallon plateau feeds 22 West African rivers.
Bossou chimps crack oil-palm nuts with stone hammers.
Djembe drums from Guinea are played from Tokyo to Toronto.
Mount Nimba's toad gives birth to live toadlets.
The 2014 Ebola outbreak began in one Guinean village.
Conakry's Grand Mosque was the largest in sub-Saharan Africa in 1982.

myths.myth: All the Guineas are one country
myths.fact: Four places share the name Guinea. Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Equatorial Guinea and Papua New Guinea are all separate countries.

myths.myth: A djembe drum is played with sticks
myths.fact: Drummers use bare hands. A djembe makes three sounds: a deep bass, a clear tone and a sharp slap.
